novel_features.name: Hidden Portfolio Rollup
novel_features.description: Find all buildings owned by the same beneficial owner across multiple LLCs
novel_features.rationale: Requires local join across county records, State SoS, and OpenCorporates to traverse entity chains and find shared beneficial ownership
novel_features.why_it_matters: When an agent needs to understand the full scope of a CRE owner's holdings hidden behind multiple shell LLCs

novel_features.name: Motivated Seller Scoring
novel_features.description: Ranked deal-sourcing list combining tax delinquency, hold duration, out-of-state ownership, and code violations into a single distress score
novel_features.rationale: Requires cross-source signal aggregation that no single API provides — county tax records, deed history, SoS entity data, and code violations all joined locally
novel_features.why_it_matters: When an agent is sourcing off-market CRE deals and needs to rank properties by likelihood of motivated seller

novel_features.name: Cold Outreach Ranking
novel_features.description: Ranked cold-outreach list with mailing addresses, registered agent info, and cross-source contact confidence scores
novel_features.rationale: Requires entity chain traversal plus contact confidence scoring across Crexi broker data, SoS registered agent, OpenCorporates officers, and enrichment sources
novel_features.why_it_matters: When an agent is building a targeted mailing or calling campaign for CRE building owners

novel_features.name: Co-Owner Network Discovery
novel_features.description: Discover hidden partnerships by finding LLCs that share officers, registered agents, or mailing addresses with a target entity
novel_features.rationale: Requires joining SOS officer and agent records across every entity in the local mirror, then mapping back to assessor parcel ownership
novel_features.why_it_matters: When an agent needs to map the full network of related entities and co-investors behind a commercial property portfolio

novel_features.name: Tax Sale Countdown
novel_features.description: Ranked list of properties approaching tax sale deadlines, giving investors a precise window to approach desperate owners
novel_features.rationale: Requires temporal computation over multi-year delinquency records combined with local jurisdiction redemption period rules
novel_features.why_it_matters: When an agent is identifying the highest-urgency motivated sellers — owners about to lose their property to tax sale

novel_features.name: Comp Gap Analysis
novel_features.description: Compare a property's assessed value against recent comparable sales to find value arbitrage opportunities
novel_features.rationale: Requires joining assessor valuation data with Crexi sold comps in a geographic radius — neither source alone has both values
novel_features.why_it_matters: When an agent is evaluating whether a property is undervalued relative to market and worth pursuing as an off-market deal

novel_features.name: Portfolio Acquisition Packager
novel_features.description: Generate a one-page dossier for a target owner's entire portfolio with property count, values, tax exposure, entity status, and contacts
novel_features.rationale: Aggregates data from assessor, SoS, Crexi, and SEC into a single document that no individual platform produces
novel_features.why_it_matters: When an agent is preparing outreach materials or meeting prep for a specific CRE portfolio owner

novel_features.name: Entity Chain Visualization
novel_features.description: Visual tree showing LLC to officers to other LLCs to beneficial owner chain from multi-source traversal
novel_features.rationale: Requires traversing entity relationships across county records, SoS filings, and OpenCorporates — no single source spans the full chain
novel_features.why_it_matters: When an agent needs to understand the corporate structure behind a commercial property to find the actual decision-maker

narrative.headline: Find who owns any commercial building, pierce the LLC veil, and surface motivated-seller signals — all from free public records stitched into a local SQLite mirror
narrative.value_prop: CRE Owner aggregates county assessor records, State Secretary of State filings, SEC EDGAR, OpenCorporates, and Crexi listings into a single local database. Compound queries across this mirror surface hidden portfolios, distress signals, and outreach targets that no individual source can produce alone.
narrative.auth_narrative: Foundation-tier commands (owner lookup, entity search, motivated scoring) work without any API keys — they query free public records. Crexi enrichment (listings, broker contacts) requires a Chrome session cookie: log in to Crexi in Chrome, then run `cre-owner-pp-cli auth login --chrome` to import the session. Optional paid hooks (Regrid, ATTOM, Trepp) are configured via environment variables when you have accounts.

quickstart.comment: Pull all data sources (parcels, owners, tax records, entities, listings) into local SQLite

quickstart.command: cre-owner-pp-cli owners lookup --address '123 Broadway, Merrillville, IN'
quickstart.comment: Look up owner of record for an address
Surface motivated sellers ranked by distress signals
Build a cold-outreach list with contacts and mailing addresses as CSV
Find every building this entity controls across all its LLCs

troubleshoots.fix: Run `sync` to refresh the local mirror. The assessor portal may have changed.
Your Crexi session cookie expired. Log in to Crexi in Chrome and re-run `auth login --chrome`.
Entity lookups are cached locally. Run `sync` first, then queries hit the local mirror instead of the API.
Some states don't publish officer data publicly. Try `entities search --query <name> --state IN` for Indiana-specific SoS lookup.

narrative.when_to_use: Use CRE Owner when you need to find who owns a commercial building, understand their full portfolio across multiple LLCs, identify motivated sellers in a market, or build cold-outreach lists with contact info. It's the right tool for CRE investors doing off-market deal sourcing, wholesalers building mailing campaigns, and brokers researching ownership for prospecting. The local SQLite mirror means compound queries work offline and don't burn API quotas.
